$comment: SHARED TEST VECTORS — the contract between the C# and TypeScript implementations
of the same validation rules.
The MySS API validates every submitted value server-side (Phase 3); the Form.io
custom components validate the same values in the browser (Phase 1). Two
implementations of one rule, in two languages, written weeks apart, will drift
unless something forces them to agree. This file is that something: both test
suites read it, so a divergence is a failing test rather than a production bug.
RULES FOR EDITING
- Every value here is SYNTHETIC. Numbers were generated to satisfy the
arithmetic; none belongs to a real person. Never paste a real SIN, PHN or
personal email address into this file.
- Adding a case means both suites must handle it. That is the point.
- `keyword` must match the keyword the implementation emits, not just the
fact of failure. Agreeing that something is invalid while disagreeing about
why still produces different messages for a citizen.
SOURCE OF THE RULES
SIN Luhn mod-10 and email format are ported from
myss-api/app/domains/registration/validators.py (BR-D1-02, BR-D1-07).
PHN mod-11 is deliberately ABSENT: that implementation includes the position-0
prefix digit in the weighted sum and its own author flagged this as unverified
against the BC Ministry of Health specification. Resolve that question before
adding PHN vectors here, or the ambiguity gets baked into two languages at once.

valid.note: space-separated, as a citizen would paste it
plus addressing is legitimate and commonly used

matching.note: case-insensitive: mail domains are, and citizens retype inconsistently
